`verus /work/rod_cutting.rs` now prints `verification results:: 10 verified, 0 errors`. The remaining output is Verus's usual trigger-selection note, not an error.

The body is a bottom-up DP over rod lengths. `dp[j]` holds the best revenue for length `j`. For each `i` from 1 to `n`, an inner loop takes the maximum over first-piece lengths `l` of `prices[l-1] + dp[i-l]`.

The proof rests on two facts the loops carry:
- **Upper bound:** every valid cut list for length `j` earns at most `dp[j]`. This is proved by splitting off the first piece with `lemma_first`.
- **Existence:** every `dp[j]` is achieved by some valid cut list. The inner loop builds this witness by prepending `l` to the witness for `dp[i-l]`.

An invariant `dp[j] <= 10000 * j` keeps the additions from overflowing `u64`.

I also added three helper lemmas (`lemma_nonneg`, `lemma_zero`, `lemma_cons`) and a helper spec function `achieves`, which wraps the existential so Verus can pick triggers for it. All edits are inside the `<helpers>`, `<proofs>` and `<code>` regions. The signature, `requires`/`ensures` and `fn main` are unchanged.
